title: XOR.DDoS_Incident_Response_aa6
description: Investigate and respond to a potential XOR.DDoS malware infection, specifically the Groundhog variant.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The organization has detected unusual network activity on its Linux servers. Initial analysis suggests a possible XOR.DDoS malware infection, specifically the Groundhog variant. Your team is responsible for investigating, analyzing, and responding to this potential cybersecurity incident.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the target server with the following credentials:
- Host: target (192.168.50.5)
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the scenario.
levels.local_content:
Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario. Use the following credentials to access the target server:
- Host: target (192.168.50.5)
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the scenario.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring the target server, you've noticed unusual network activity. Investigate the running services on the target server to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services.
levels.solution: To identify suspicious services, you can use the `systemctl list-units --type=service` command to list all running services. Look for any unusual or unexpected services, such as `bkd.service`. The final flag is `bkd.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the systemd services and look for any unusual or unexpected services.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: Now that you've identified a suspicious service, investigate its network activity. Determine which network port is used for the suspicious communication.
levels.solution: To identify the network port used for the suspicious communication, you can use the `ss -tulnp` command to list all open ports and their associated processes. Look for the port associated with the `bkd.service`. The final flag is `4444`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use network monitoring tools to identify open ports and their associated processes.

levels.title: Lateral Movement Investigation
levels.content: Investigate the target server for any signs of lateral movement. Identify any file transfers or remote execution used to move between hosts.
levels.solution: To investigate lateral movement, you can check the system logs using the `journalctl -u payload-transfer.service` command to look for any unusual file transfers or remote command executions. The final flag is `payload-transfer.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the system logs and look for any unusual file transfers or remote command executions.
